issues.claim: Kubernetes passes the CPU limit to the Linux kernel as a CFS quota: in every scheduler period (100 ms by default) ... A limit is a hard ceiling that applies even when the node is idle ... the Pod gets the Burstable QoS class

issues.claim: The minimum number of thread pool threads and the number of server GC heaps depend on that number ... DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT can override the processor count
issues.problem: The garbage collector config excerpt is cut off before any statement about heap count or processor count. Nothing in it says the thread pool minimum is derived from ProcessorCount or mentions DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT. The claims are plausible and I believe they are correct, but neither excerpt supports them. The ProcessorCount excerpt confirms only the round-up of the CPU limit.
issues.suggestedFix: Cite the runtime-config pages that document DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT and the thread pool minimum threads (ThreadPool.GetMinThreads / System.Threading.ThreadPool.MinThreads), or drop the explicit DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT claim.

issues.claim: they use up the quota in 25 ms ... (request handling, JIT, parallel garbage collection) ... the garbage collector loses its parallelism
issues.problem: Parallel GC threads and GC heaps exist only with server GC, which is not the default for every ASP.NET Core app (workstation concurrent GC is the default unless configured). The text implies server GC without saying so. The same applies to the RU text.
issues.suggestedFix: Add 'if server GC is enabled' to the sentence about GC heaps and parallel GC, in both locales.
